text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended with pared gains after an erratic session. July added $40 to close at $2,150 per tonne. September closed at $2,190 per tonne, a gain of $55. Traders said that a further recovery is possible after the massive sell-off over the last few days. Arabica futures in New York closed sharply higher after a volatile session. July closed 10.25 cents/lb higher at $264.20 cents/lb. September closed at 233.05 cents/lb, a gain of 8.50 cents/lb. Fundamentals remain constructive and low inventory levels in consuming and producing countries will keep prices well supported. Some traders do not exclude that the market will retest recent highs.
UNITED STATES - US certified coffee stocks fell by 2,250 bags on June 2 to 45,985 bags, down from 48,235 bags the previous day. There were 570 bags pending grading in New York and 750 bags in Miami.

BRAZIL - Brazil's coffee exports under the ACPC retention scheme, should not be more than 6 million 60-kg bags between January and June. However, according to official figures received by May 30, the country had already shipped 6.3 million bags and according to export registrations received to May 16, a further 469,815 bags had been registered for June export.

COLOMBIA - Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said Colombia was opening 'unlimited' coffee registrations for July/August, a period in which the country was expected to export 2.5 million 60-kg bags of coffee. This means that private exporters and the Coffee Federation are authorized to export all the coffee they can obtain.

SOUTH KOREA - Korea imported 80,000 bags of coffee in December 1996, 16 per cent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 995,500 bags, 8 per cent less than was imported in 1995. Main suppliers of green coffee in 1996 were Honduras (128,800 vs 114,800 bags), Colombia (121,400 vs 131,600 bags) and Indonesia (242,200 vs 95,700 bags). The country exported 74,300 bags of coffee in 1996, 50 per cent more than was exported the previous year.

CZECH REPUBLIC - Coffee imports in January/February 1997 totalled 117,900 bags of which 90,100 bags green coffee, 7,900 bags roast and ground and 19,900 bags solubles. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/February 1997 were Uganda (10,400 bags), Brazil (21,600 bags), Colombia (10,100 bags) and Vietnam (10,600 bags). Coffee exports in January/February 1997 reached 11,600 bags.

RUSSIA - Russia imported 324,300 bags of coffee in January/March 1997 of which 14,700 bags green coffee, 24,900 bags roast and ground and 284,700 bags solubles. Main suppliers of solubles in January/March 1997 were France (23,900 bags), Germany (23,200 bags), Brazil (43,900 bags) and India (102,700 bags).
